lessons.text: If a command's output comes back empty, re-run that same command unchanged; do not fall back to a tool the instructions forbid (e.g. piping `cat <datafile>` through wc/grep) to diagnose it.
lessons.evidence: In the 0wluwrkj.log chain task, `cat 455pw2ah.log` appeared to return nothing, so I ran `cat 455pw2ah.log | wc -l; cat 455pw2ah.log | grep -c .`, breaking the explicit cat-only rule; a plain re-run showed the content fine.

lessons.text: Reading a long file chain under a token budget: after each `cat`, extract only the two useful lines (id/severity and next file) into one running note, then delete the raw dump block from the context file before the next read, so the raw dumps never accumulate.
lessons.evidence: In the 0wluwrkj.log chain session, 8 files of ~300 lines each (~24KB per dump) were cat'ed into context; pruning the dumps after each read is what kept the file at ~1-8KB and the chain finishable within 32k tokens.

lessons.text: When pruning the context file, select blocks by their known `[[CTX <id> ...]]` ids in a script and keep the user's task/output-format block verbatim; never prune by content keywords and never by block position, since both can drop the requirements or leave duplicate notes.
lessons.evidence: Same keyword-prune failure as before, plus this session's prune kept the task block only because it happened to be block index 0 (`blocks[0]`), which would have dropped the requirements if any other message had come first.

lessons.text: Chains of `KEY_<n>` / `NEXT FILE:` data files can be padded: a file may contain hundreds of noise lines with the one `KEY_<n>` and one `NEXT FILE:` line buried anywhere inside. After the single `cat`, scan the whole dump for exactly one of each, take the pair into the note, and delete the dump — a padded file is the biggest single context cost in these tasks and nothing else from it is needed.
lessons.evidence: In this session the last file 8ngj7mh5.log was ~300 numbered lines of random words with `KEY_9 = OMPOBTS2` after line 0068 and `NEXT FILE: none` after 0199; only those two lines mattered, and that one dump dominated the 251k-token cost.
